title: Chest Pain: General Information

body: Chest pain has many possible causes, ranging from muscle strain to serious heart or lung conditions. Because some causes are life-threatening, chest pain is always taken seriously in a medical setting, even when it later turns out to be minor.

Pain that comes with shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, or pain spreading to the arm, jaw, or back can be a sign of a heart attack. This combination should be treated as a medical emergency regardless of the person's age or fitness level, since heart attacks do not always present with 'classic' textbook symptoms, especially in women and older adults.

Chest pain that is sharp, worsens with breathing or movement, and is not accompanied by other cardiac warning signs is more commonly linked to musculoskeletal strain, acid reflux, or anxiety — but this should still be confirmed by a clinician rather than assumed, particularly if it is a new or unfamiliar sensation.
